text: And after all the weather was ideal. <break time="0.8s" /> For they could not have had a more perfect day for a garden party. <break time="0.8s" /> If they had ordered it. <break time="0.8s" /> The air was windless and warm. <break time="0.8s" /> The sky was without a cloud. <break time="0.8s" /> And the gardener had been up since dawn. <break time="0.8s" /> Mowing the lawns and sweeping them. <break time="0.8s" /> Until they seemed to shine. <break time="0.8s" /> Before breakfast was even over the men came to put up the marquee. <break time="0.8s" /> And Missus Sheridan. <break time="0.8s" /> Who wanted the children to arrange everything themselves. <break time="0.8s" /> Told them to treat her as an honored guest. <break time="0.8s" /> Laura who was considered the artistic one in the family. <break time="0.8s" /> Ran out to meet the four workmen. <break time="0.8s" /> Still holding a piece of bread and butter. <break time="0.8s" /> In her hand. <break time="0.8s" /> She tried to sound businesslike. <break time="0.8s" /> By copying her mothers voice. <break time="0.8s" /> But it sounded so affected. <break time="0.8s" /> That she felt ashamed. <break time="0.8s" /> And stammered like a little girl instead. <break time="0.8s" /> When she suggested the lily lawn. <break time="0.8s" /> The tall, lanky, freckled workman looked around. <break time="0.8s" /> And said that a marquee there. <break time="0.8s" /> Would not be conspicuous enough. <break time="0.8s" /> In the end he chose a place. <break time="0.8s" /> Against the karaka trees. <break time="0.8s" /> And Laura was sorry. <break time="0.8s" /> Because the trees. <break time="0.8s" /> With their broad gleaming leaves. <break time="0.8s" /> And clusters of yellow fruit. <break time="0.8s" /> Would be hidden. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the tall workman pinched a sprig of lavender. <break time="0.8s" /> And smelled it. <break time="0.8s" /> And Laura, deeply charmed. <break time="0.8s" /> Wondered how many of the men she knew. <break time="0.8s" /> Would ever have done such a thing. <break time="0.8s" /> It was all the fault. <break time="0.8s" /> Of these absurd class distinctions. <break time="0.8s" /> She decided. <break time="0.8s" /> And to show how much at home she felt. <break time="0.8s" /> She took a big bite. <break time="0.8s" /> Of her bread and butter.
